# Offline use

This is an original concise problem sheet, not a copy of Codeforces statements.
It contains the information needed for an offline attempt and each official
URL. Before submitting, read the official page: it controls any detail not
present here. Ratings are approximate guideposts, not prerequisites.

Each rung also has an original, locally judgeable companion package under
`problems/`; see [the companion index](OFFLINE_COMPANIONS.md). The companion
is a separate exercise for the same course skill, with skeletons, references,
and tests. It is intentionally not a copy of the linked Codeforces statement.

# Gate 1: foundations

## 1. 71A -- Way Too Long Words (800)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/71/A>

For each of at most 100 lowercase words (length at most 100), print it
unchanged when its length is at most 10. Otherwise print its first character,
the number of characters strictly between the ends, and its last character.
Output one transformed word per input word.

## 2. 4C -- Registration System (1300)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/4/C>

Process up to `10^5` requested lowercase names. A first request for a name
prints `OK`. A later request prints that base name followed by the smallest
positive suffix that has not previously been issued, and the issued name also
becomes occupied. Output one response per request.

## 3. 363B -- Fence (1100)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/363/B>

Given `n <= 1.5 * 10^5` positive heights and `k`, choose `k` consecutive
positions with minimum total height. Print a 1-indexed starting position; any
minimum is accepted. The fence is a line, not a cycle.

## 4. 279B -- Books (1400)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/279/B>

Given at most `10^5` positive reading times and a time budget `t`, choose a
contiguous block of books whose sum is at most `t`. Print the maximum possible
number of books. An individual book may already exceed the budget.

## 5. 158B -- Taxi (1100)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/158/B>

Up to `10^5` groups, each of size 1 through 4, must ride in taxis of capacity
4. Groups cannot split, but different groups may share a taxi. Print the
minimum taxi count.

## 6. 706B -- Interesting Drink (1100)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/706/B>

Store up to `10^5` drink prices. For each of up to `10^5` budget queries,
print how many drinks cost no more than that budget. Prices and budgets fit in
ordinary signed 32-bit input values; answers are counts.

# Gate 2: graph, DP, math, and geometry

## 7. 520B -- Two Buttons (1400)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/520/B>

Starting from positive integer `n`, reach positive integer `m` using only
`x -> 2x` and `x -> x-1`. With `n,m <= 10^4`, print the fewest operations.
The intermediate values may exceed `m`, but a finite state bound must be
justified.

## 8. 455A -- Boredom (1500)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/455/A>

From a multiset of at most `10^5` integers, repeatedly choose a value `x`, add
`x` to the score, and remove every occurrence of `x-1`, `x`, and `x+1`.
Maximize the total. Values are positive and bounded by `10^5`.

## 9. 300C -- Beautiful Numbers (1800)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/300/C>

Count length-`n` decimal strings whose digits are only `a` and `b` and whose
digit sum, written in decimal, itself uses only `a` and `b`. The input has
`1 <= a < b <= 9` and `n <= 10^6`, so factorials modulo `1_000_000_007` are
required. Print the count modulo that prime.

## 10. 166B -- Polygons (2100, geometry challenge)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/166/B>

You receive a strictly convex outer polygon A and an arbitrary simple inner
polygon B, both listed clockwise with integer coordinates. Decide whether all
of B lies strictly inside A. A vertex of B on A's boundary is not allowed.

## 11. 20C -- Dijkstra? (1900)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/20/C>

In an undirected graph with up to `10^5` vertices and edges and positive edge
weights, print one shortest path from vertex 1 to vertex `n`, or `-1` if none
exists. The path, not just its distance, is required.

## 12. 161D -- Distance in Tree (1800)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/161/D>

For a tree with up to `5 * 10^4` vertices and a distance `k <= 500`, count
unordered pairs of distinct vertices whose simple-path distance is exactly
`k`. A direct BFS from every vertex is too slow.

# Gate 3: compressed state and data structures

## 13. 580D -- Kefa and Dishes (1800)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/580/D>

Choose exactly `m` of at most 18 dishes and order the chosen dishes. Each dish
has a base satisfaction, and selected ordered pairs add a bonus when the first
dish immediately precedes the second. Maximize total satisfaction.

## 14. 1245D -- Shichikuji and Power Grid (1900)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1245/D>

For up to 2000 cities, either build a station in a city or connect cities by
wires. Station and Manhattan-distance wire costs are supplied. Make every city
receive power at minimum cost, then print the chosen stations and wires.

## 15. 271D -- Good Substrings (1800)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/271/D>

Given a lowercase string of length at most 1500, a 26-character good/bad mask,
and `k`, count distinct substrings containing at most `k` bad characters.
Equal substrings from different positions count once.

## 16. 61E -- Enemy Is Weak (1900)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/61/E>

For an array of up to `10^6` distinct values, count triples `i < j < k` with
`a[i] > a[j] > a[k]`. The answer can require 64 bits.

## 17. 86D -- Powerful Array (2200)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/86/D>

For up to `2 * 10^5` range queries, compute
`sum(value * frequency(value)^2)` over each subarray. Values are bounded, but
recomputing every query from scratch is too slow. Print answers in query order.

# Gate 4: reductions and optimization

## 18. 498C -- Array and Operations (2100)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/498/C>

Given numbers on odd and even indexed vertices and allowed odd-even links,
perform as many operations as possible. An operation chooses a linked pair and
any common divisor greater than one, then divides both current numbers by that
divisor. Find the maximum number of operations.

## 19. 319C -- Kalila and Dimna in the Logging Industry (2100)

Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/319/C>

The official story supplies strictly increasing tree heights `a` and strictly
decreasing recharge costs `b`, with `n <= 10^5`. Compute the minimum total
cutting cost under the stated transition rules. The answer can exceed 32-bit
integer range.

# Gate 5: hard data structures and tree techniques

## 20. 786B -- Legacy
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/786/B>

Maintain a directed weighted graph under edge additions from one vertex to one
vertex, from one vertex to every vertex in an interval, and from every vertex
in an interval to one vertex. Then print shortest distances from a source.

## 21. 191C -- Fools and Roads
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/191/C>

Given a tree and many vertex pairs, count for every edge how many requested
simple paths use it. Print counts in input-edge order.

## 22. 208E -- Blood Cousins
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/208/E>

In a rooted forest, query a vertex `v` and integer `p`: count other vertices at
the depth of `v` whose `p`-th ancestor equals the `p`-th ancestor of `v`.

## 23. 375D -- Tree and Queries
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/375/D>

Each tree vertex has a color. For every `(v, k)`, count colors occurring at
least `k` times inside the subtree of `v`.

## 24. 600E -- Lomsat gelral
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/600/E>

For every tree vertex, sum all color values whose frequency is maximum in its
subtree.

## 25. 877E -- Danil and a Part-time Job
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/877/E>

Root a tree. Toggle all binary values in a queried subtree or report a queried
subtree sum.

## 26. 242E -- XOR on Segment
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/242/E>

Maintain an array under range xor updates and range-sum queries.

## 27. 103D -- Time to Raid Cowavans
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/103/D>

For each `(a, b)`, sum `a[a] + a[a+b] + a[a+2b] + ...` while indices remain
in bounds.

# Gate 6: expert modeling and offline structures

## 28. 1000F -- One Occurrence
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1000/F>

For every range `[l, r]`, print any value occurring exactly once in that range,
or zero when none exists.

## 29. 240F -- TorCoder
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/240/F>

Maintain a lowercase string while substring operations sort one selected range
in increasing or decreasing order. Output the final string.

## 30. 343D -- Water Tree
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/343/D>

Root a tree and support filling a subtree, emptying a root-to-vertex path, and
querying whether one vertex is filled.

## 31. 1209E2 -- Rotate Columns
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1209/E2>

Choose cyclic rotations of selected matrix columns so every row takes one value
and the resulting total is maximum.

## 32. 1416C -- XOR Inverse
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1416/C>

Choose one xor mask for all array values to minimize the transformed inversion
count. Output the count and one valid mask.

## 33. 13E -- Holes
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/13/E>

Array values define jumps `i -> i+a[i]`. Support point updates and queries for
the number of jumps to leave the array and the final in-array position.

## 34. 342E -- Xenia and Tree
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/342/E>

Initially one tree vertex is red. Repeatedly color vertices red or query the
nearest-red distance from a vertex.

## 35. 895C -- Square Subsets
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/895/C>

Count nonempty subsets of a bounded-value multiset whose product is a perfect
square, modulo the required prime.

## 36. 868F -- Yet Another Minimization Problem
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/868/F>

Partition an array into exactly `k` nonempty segments. Segment cost is the
number of equal-value pairs in it; minimize total cost.

## 37. 1292C -- Xenon's Attack on the Gangs
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1292/C>

Choose two tree vertices and maximize the product of the endpoint component
sizes obtained by cutting toward the other endpoint along their path.

## 38. 613D -- Kingdom and its Cities
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/613/D>

For each marked set of tree vertices, delete as few other vertices as possible
so no component contains two marked vertices, or report impossibility.

## 39. 1110F -- Nearest Leaf
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1110/F>

For a weighted rooted tree, answer minimum-distance-to-leaf queries restricted
to a DFS-order interval of leaves.

## 40. 587C -- Duff in the Army
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/587/C>

People occupy tree vertices. For each path, print the smallest few person ids
on that path, up to the requested limit.

# Gate 7: red-level optimization

## 41. 786C -- Till I Collapse
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/786/C>

For every `k`, partition the array greedily into the fewest segments containing
at most `k` distinct values and print all answers.

## 42. 1093G -- Multidimensional Queries
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1093/G>

Maintain points in dimension at most five under point updates; for each index
range, output the maximum Manhattan distance between two points in it.

## 43. 321E -- Ciel and Gondolas
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/321/E>

Partition a binary compatibility matrix into exactly `k` contiguous groups and
minimize the sum of group-square disagreement costs.

## 44. 896C -- Willem, Chtholly and Seniorious
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/896/C>

Support range assignment, range addition, kth-smallest, and modular power-sum
queries on the statement's generated array.

## 45. 833B -- The Bakery
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/833/B>

Split an array into exactly `k` nonempty segments. A segment scores its number
of distinct values; maximize total score.

## 46. 311B -- Cats Transport
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/311/B>

Cats arrive at stations on a line. A limited number of buses carry consecutive
groups; minimize total waiting time.

## 47. 55D -- Beautiful Numbers
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/55/D>

For each interval, count positive integers divisible by every nonzero decimal
digit they contain.

## 48. 840D -- Destiny
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/840/D>

For each range and integer `k`, find a value occurring more than
`length / k` times, or report that no such value exists.

## 49. 911G -- Mass Change Queries
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/911/G>

Apply range operations that replace every occurrence of one value by another,
then print the resulting array.

## 50. 1100F -- Ivan and Burgers
Official: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1100/F>

For each array range, choose any subset of its values to maximize their xor.

# Offline blind capstone

## D. Ribbon Cuts -- Codeforces 189A companion

Official companion: <https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/189/A>

Given a ribbon of length `n` and three permitted positive piece lengths `a`,
`b`, and `c`, use the whole ribbon and maximize the number of pieces. Print
`-1` when no exact cutting exists. The local version has `n <= 200000` and is
also available in `problems/d_ribbon_cuts` with fixed tests for offline work.
